title: The Dice Tower
tagline: for loops, and dice that lie the same way twice
hints: `for (int i = 1; i <= 10; ++i) { ... }` packs the three parts of a while loop onto one line: set up, test, step.
Declare `hits` and `total` BEFORE the for loop. Anything declared inside is destroyed at the closing brace.
Call `roll(6)` exactly once per pass and store it: `int r = roll(6);`. If you call it twice you get two different numbers and your log will not match your total.
`if (r >= 4) { ++hits; }` and `total += r;` both go inside the same loop body, after the roll.
